title: Separatedness of a representable Hilbert scheme
statement: Let $X\to S$ be a separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-morphism-conventions] and let $d\geq0$. If the Hilbert functor $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{X/S}$ [def-pc-hilb-functor] is representable by a scheme $H_d$, then $H_d\to S$ is separated [def-pc-morphism-conventions].

source.place: Stacks Project, Picard Schemes of Curves, Lemma 44.2.8, Tag 0B98 (pic-lemma-hilb-d-separated)

proof.text: Write $H=H_d$ and put $P=H\times_S H$. Pull back the universal object of $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{X/S}(H)$ along the two projections $P\to H$; by functoriality of the Hilbert functor [lem-pc-hilb-functorial] this gives $Z_1,Z_2\in\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{X/S}(P)$, i.e. closed subschemes of $X_P$ that are finite locally free of degree $d$ over $P$, and for every $T'\to P$ their pullbacks $Z_{1,T'},Z_{2,T'}$ are the corresponding elements of $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{X/S}(T')$. Apply the closed-containment-locus statement [lem-pc-hilb-containment-locus] with $T=P$ to $(Z,W)=(Z_1,Z_2)$ and to $(Z,W)=(Z_2,Z_1)$ (each $Z_i\hookrightarrow X_P$ is a closed immersion and each is finite locally free of degree $d$ over $P$); this gives closed subschemes $P_{12},P_{21}\subseteq P$, and $T'\to P$ factors through the closed subscheme $P_{12}\cap P_{21}$ if and only if $Z_{1,T'}\subseteq Z_{2,T'}$ and $Z_{2,T'}\subseteq Z_{1,T'}$.

source.place: Picard Schemes of Curves, Lemma 44.2.8, label lemma-hilb-d-separated, Tag 0B98; proof, containment loci

proof.text: For every $T'\to P$, since $H$ represents $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{X/S}$ [def-pc-hilb-functor], $T'\to P$ factors through the diagonal $\Delta:H\to P$ if and only if $Z_{1,T'}=Z_{2,T'}$ as elements of $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{X/S}(T')$. Equality of closed subschemes of $X_{T'}$ is equivalent to mutual containment, so $\Delta$ and $P_{12}\cap P_{21}\hookrightarrow P$ represent the same subfunctor of $P$; by Yoneda $\Delta$ is isomorphic over $P$ to this closed immersion, hence is a closed immersion. By the diagonal definition of separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism], $H_d\to S$ is separated.

source.place: Picard Schemes of Curves, Lemma 44.2.8, label lemma-hilb-d-separated, Tag 0B98; proof, diagonal
